scopeClasses.name: Non sensitive scopes
scopeClasses.description: Sign in and per file access. No scope verification. Brand verification only if you want your name and logo shown.

scopeClasses.name: Sensitive scopes
scopeClasses.description: Scope verification required before more than 100 users can connect. Google states 10 business days; developers report six weeks or more in 2026.

scopeClasses.name: Restricted scopes
scopeClasses.description: Scope verification plus an annual CASA security assessment by a paid third party assessor. Google states 6 weeks for the verification alone.

claims.text: Google requires three types of verification for apps that access user data through OAuth: brand, sensitive scope and restricted scope.
claims.label: documented
claims.quote: There are three types of verification that Google requires to access user data via OAuth.

claims.text: Apps that request sensitive scopes must pass scope verification before external users beyond the cap can connect.
claims.label: documented
claims.quote: Failure to get your app verified for sensitive and/or restricted scopes.

claims.text: Apps that request restricted scopes must pass scope verification.
claims.label: documented
claims.quote: Failure to get your app verified for sensitive and/or restricted scopes.

claims.text: Google states 2 to 3 business days for brand verification.
claims.label: documented
claims.quote: 2-3 Business days

claims.text: Google states 10 business days for sensitive scope verification.
claims.label: documented
claims.quote: 10 Business days

claims.text: Google states 6 weeks for restricted scope verification.
claims.label: documented

claims.label: documented

steps.title: Classify the scopes you need: non sensitive, sensitive or restricted
steps.detail: This decides everything below. Gmail read and modify scopes are restricted. Pick the narrowest class that does the job; drive.file instead of drive, for example.
inputs: The exact scope list your agent needs

steps.title: Sign in to Google Cloud, create a project and open the Google Auth Platform
inputs: A Google account; a Workspace organization if you want the Internal user type

steps.title: Configure the consent screen with the External user type, your app name, support email, homepage, privacy policy and authorized domains
steps.detail: The homepage must sit on a domain you own and the privacy policy on that same domain.

steps.title: Verify your authorized domains in Google Search Console
inputs: Access to the domain's DNS or site

steps.title: Create the OAuth client ID, add your redirect URIs and store the client ID and secret in your auth config
inputs: Redirect URI from your auth config

steps.title: Keep the app in Testing while you build, with up to 100 test users whose grants expire every 7 days
Publish to production. With non sensitive scopes you are done; with sensitive or restricted scopes you can ship to 100 users while verification runs
steps.detail: Users see an unverified app warning until verification passes, and the 100 user limit does not lift on its own.

steps.title: Write the scope justification for each sensitive or restricted scope
steps.detail: Name the feature each scope powers and why a narrower scope will not do. An insufficient justification is a stated rejection reason.
inputs: A sentence per scope tying it to a visible feature

steps.title: Record the demo video: the full flow from sign in through the complete consent screen to the feature using the data
Submit for verification from the Verification Center and answer Trust and Safety emails the same day
steps.detail: Google states 10 business days for sensitive scopes and 6 weeks for restricted, and says the estimates are not guaranteed. Developers in 2026 report six weeks or more for sensitive scopes.

steps.title: For restricted scopes: book a CASA assessor, pass the assessment, and submit the Letter of Validation
steps.detail: You pay the assessor. Reported prices run from about USD 700 to USD 3,000 or more. The assessment repeats every year.

steps.title: Put annual re verification and the assessment renewal on the calendar

playbooks.symptom: The 101st user cannot connect and existing users see an unverified app warning.
playbooks.cause: Your app requests sensitive or restricted scopes and is not verified. The 100 new user limit holds until verification.
playbooks.fix: Submit for verification now. While you wait, nothing lifts the cap; the Internal user type is only an option for your own Workspace organization.

playbooks.symptom: Verification sits in review for weeks past Google's stated 10 business days.
playbooks.cause: Google calls its durations estimates and developers in 2026 report six weeks or more, often at the privacy policy requirements stage.
playbooks.fix: Check that the privacy policy is on the homepage's domain, that Search Console verification is complete, and reply to every Trust and Safety email the same day. Plan launches on the reported figure, not the stated one.

playbooks.symptom: The verification request was rejected over scope justification.
playbooks.cause: The justification did not tie each scope to a visible feature or a narrower scope would do.
playbooks.fix: Rewrite the justification per scope, drop scopes you cannot defend, and show the feature in the demo video.

playbooks.symptom: Test users are asked to consent again every week.
playbooks.cause: Authorizations granted to test users while the app is in Testing expire after seven days.
playbooks.fix: Expected behaviour. Publish to production once the consent screen is complete; the 100 user cap still applies for sensitive and restricted scopes until verification.
